sections.title: Detailed Brief Overview
rows: The **Maurya Dynasty** (मौर्य वंश) was the first largest and most powerful ancient Indian imperial power founded by **Chandragupta Maurya**.
Ruled from **322 BCE to 185 BCE** (Total duration of approximately 137 years).
Centered in **Magadha** (modern-day Bihar/Gangetic plains) and expanded to cover most of the **Indian subcontinent**, parts of modern-day Afghanistan and Baluchistan.
Key figures include **Chandragupta Maurya**, his mentor **Kautilya (Chanakya)**, son **Bindusara**, and grandson **Emperor Ashoka**.
Established the first **pan-Indian empire**, introduced centralized administration, standardized coinage, and spread **Buddhism** globally through Ashoka's **Dhamma**.
Detailed in **Arthashastra** and **Indica**; highly organized bureaucracy, efficient espionage system, extensive trade networks, and magnificent stone architecture.
High-yielding static GK topic in UPSSSC PET history syllabus; questions frequently asked on **Edicts, Kalinga War, Chanakya, and Foreign Travelers**.

Literary sources include **Kautilya's Arthashastra**, **Megasthenes' Indica**, **Visakhadatta's Mudrarakshasa**, and Buddhist texts like **Mahavamsa** and **Dipavamsa**; Archaeological sources include **Ashokan Edicts**.

items.title: 1. Foundation of the Maurya Empire & Chandragupta Maurya (322–298 BCE)
items.content:
• Overthrew the last Nanda king, **Dhana Nanda**, with the help of **Chanakya (Kautilya)** in **322 BCE**.
• Defeated **Seleucus Nicator** (Alexander's general) in **305 BCE**, acquiring territories of Kabul, Kandahar, Herat, and Baluchistan.
• Greek ambassador **Megasthenes** visited his court at **Pataliputra** and wrote the book **Indica**.
• Embraced **Jainism** in his later years and abdicated the throne in favor of his son **Bindusara**.
• Performed **Santhara** (Sallekhana - fasting unto death) at **Shravanabelagola** (Karnataka).
• **Mnemonic for Rulers Sequence:** **C**handragupta **B**indsusara **A**shoka **D**asaratha **S**ampati **B**rihadratha (**C**ool **B**oys **A**lways **D**o **S**mart **B**usiness).

items.title: 2. Bindusara 'Amitraghata' (298–273 BCE)
items.content:
• Son and successor of **Chandragupta Maurya**.
• Known to the Greeks as **Amitrochates**, which translates to **Amitraghata** (Slayer of foes).
• Patronized the **Ajivika sect**.
• Antiochus I (Seleucid king) sent ambassador **Deimachus** to his court.
• Pliny records that Egyptian king Ptolemy Philadelphus sent **Dionysius** as an ambassador to Bindusara's court.
• Faced a major rebellion in **Taxila** which was successfully suppressed by his son **Ashoka**.

items.title: 3. Emperor Ashoka the Great (268–232 BCE)
items.content:
• Initially known as **Chandashoka** (Cruel Ashoka) due to ruthless succession wars against his brothers.
• Fought the historic **Kalinga War** in **261 BCE** (8th year of his coronation).
• Profoundly moved by the massive bloodshed, he embraced **Buddhism** under the guidance of **Upagupta**.
• Changed his epithet to **Dhammasoka** (Pious Ashoka) and propagated **Dhamma**.
• Sent Buddhist missionaries (including his children **Mahendra** and **Sanghamitra**) to **Sri Lanka** and Central Asia.
• **Mnemonic for Ashoka's Edict Language:** **P**ra-Me-Gr-A (**P**rakrit in **Me**erut/Major Edicts, **G**reek/Aramaic in **A**fghanistan).

items.title: 4. Ashokan Edicts and Inscriptions
items.content:
• Deciphered for the first time by **James Prinsep** in **1837**.
• Written mostly in **Prakrit language** and **Brahmi script** (North-Western scripts used Kharosthi; Afghanistan region used Greek and Aramaic).
• Divided into **Major Rock Edicts** (14 in number), **Minor Rock Edicts**, **Separate Kalinga Edicts**, and **Pillar Edicts**.
• **Major Rock Edict XIII** explicitly describes the horrific details and consequences of the **Kalinga War**.
• **Major Rock Edict VII** promotes tolerance towards all religious sects.
• **Rummindei Pillar Inscription** records Ashoka's visit to Lumbini (birthplace of Buddha) and reduction of land revenue (Bhaga) to **1/8th**.

items.title: 5. Maurya Administration and Economy
items.content:
• Highly centralized bureaucratic empire headed by the **Emperor**, assisted by the **Mantriparishad** (Council of Ministers).
• **Tirthas:** Highest category of officials numbering **18** (e.g., Samaharta - collector general, Sannidhata - treasurer).
• **Adhyakshas:** Superintendents controlling various economic departments.
• **Spies:** Known as **Gudhapurushas**, forming a vast espionage network.
• **Provincial Division:** Empire divided into provinces governed by **Kumaras** (royal princes).
• **Revenue System:** Land revenue (**Bhaga**) was the main source of income, generally fixed at **1/6th** of the total produce.

items.title: 6. Decline of the Maurya Dynasty
items.content:
• Last ruler was **Brihadratha**, who was assassinated in **185 BCE** by his commander-in-chief **Pushyamitra Shunga**.
• Pushyamitra Shunga founded the **Shunga Dynasty**.
• Reasons for decline include **Ashoka's pacifist policies**, heavy financial burden of the standing army and vast bureaucracy, oppression by provincial governors, and weak later rulers.
• **Mnemonic for Last Ruler:** **B**rihadratha was **B**attered (**B-B**).

items.term: Trick 1: Sequence of First Three Rulers
items.definition: Remember **CAB** — **C**handragupta, **A**shoka (skip one mentally), or **C**handragupta -> **B**indusara -> **A**shoka. Sequence: **C-B-A** (Reverse of alphabet).
Kalinga War happened in **261 BCE**. Remember: **2+6+1 = 9**, and Ashoka's coronation was in **273 BCE** minus **12 years** approx to war.
Remember **James Prinsep** deciphered Brahmi in **1837**. Trick: **James Bond (007)** + **Prinsep (Prince)** read the secret king's code in **1837**.
Remember **CM-BD**: **C**handragupta had **M**egasthenes; **B**indusara had **D**eimachus & **D**ionysius.
Provincial capitals: **Taxila** (North), **Ujjain** (West), **Suvarnagiri** (South), **Tosali** (East). Acronym: **T-U-S-T** (Trust).
Kautilya's **Panyadhyaksha** (Trade), **Suryadhyaksha** (Agriculture), **Navadhyaksha** (Ships). Root word **'Adhyaksha'** means head/supervisor.

Students confuse Ashoka's personal belief with state religion. Ashoka personally embraced **Buddhism**, but he never made Buddhism the state religion; he propagated **Dhamma** (moral ethics for all religions).
Do not confuse **Chanakya** (Prime minister and author of Arthashastra) with **Megasthenes** (Greek ambassador and author of Indica).
The Kalinga War was **not** fought at the start of Ashoka's reign. It was fought in the **8th year after his coronation** (in **261 BCE**, whereas he ascended the throne in **268 BCE**).

items.term: Mistake 4: Script and Language of Edicts
items.definition: All Ashokan edicts are **not** in Brahmi script. Northwest edicts are in **Kharosthi**, and Afghanistan inscriptions are in **Greek and Aramaic**.
Students sometimes confuse **Chandragupta Maurya** with **Chandragupta I** of the Gupta Dynasty. Maurya founded the empire in 322 BCE, while Gupta ruler ruled in 4th Century CE.
The last ruler was **Brihadratha**, not Ashoka or Dasaratha. He was killed by **Pushyamitra Shunga**.
Founded in **322 BCE** by **Chandragupta Maurya** after defeating Dhana Nanda with Chanakya's guidance.
**Pataliputra** was the magnificent imperial capital situated at the confluence of the Ganga and Son rivers.
**Indica** by Megasthenes gives detailed accounts of Pataliputra municipal administration and Indian society.
Authored by **Kautilya (Chanakya)**, it is a master treatise on statecraft, political strategy, and economics.
Known as **Amitraghata**; maintained diplomatic ties with the Hellenistic world and patronized the **Ajivika sect**.
The **Kalinga War (261 BCE)** caused immense bloodshed, leading Ashoka to embrace Buddhism and policy of non-violence.
Ashoka's **Dhamma** was a code of social conduct, tolerance, and morality, not a distinct religious faith.
Ashokan inscriptions were first successfully deciphered by **James Prinsep in 1837**.
Ashoka patronized the **3rd Buddhist Council** held at Pataliputra around **250 BCE**.
Key architecture includes monolithic pillars, polished stone pillars, **Sanchi Stupa**, and Barabar rock-cut caves.
Ended in **185 BCE** when commander **Pushyamitra Shunga** assassinated Brihadratha.

upscNotes.content: UPSSSC PET frequently asks direct questions on authors and their books (e.g., Arthashastra by Kautilya, Indica by Megasthenes, Mudrarakshasa by Visakhadatta). Memorize this book-author mapping thoroughly.
Pay special attention to the matching questions: Match Ashokan Pillar Edicts/Locations with modern states. Focus on Sarnath, Sanchi, Lumbini, and Kalinga (Odisha).

Trap: Examiners often trap students by stating 'Ashoka converted India into a Buddhist state.' Remember, Ashoka remained tolerant of all sects (Brahmanism, Ajivikas, Jainism) and promoted universal Dhamma.
Trap: Dates in ancient Indian history can be tricky. Remember Maurya timeline is in **BCE** (counting backwards: 322 BCE to 185 BCE).

keyTakeaways: Chandragupta Maurya founded the Maurya Empire in 322 BCE with Chanakya's support.
Megasthenes' 'Indica' and Kautilya's 'Arthashastra' are the primary literary sources for Mauryan administration.
Emperor Ashoka fought the Kalinga War in 261 BCE, which deeply transformed his governance toward Dhamma and Buddhism.
James Prinsep deciphered Ashokan Brahmi inscriptions in 1837.
Ashoka propagated Dhamma, built stupas, and sent missionaries abroad including his children to Sri Lanka.
The empire declined after Ashoka and ended in 185 BCE when Brihadratha was killed by Pushyamitra Shunga.
